Hi Alex / Priya —

Congratulations and welcome aboard. Attached is a first-draft Execution MAP (Execution_MAP_v0.1.xlsx) that folds in the canary, migration, and training milestones we discussed during the contract close. Goal here is to capture a firm 6-week close-to-live sequence with clear owners and acceptance criteria.

Key asks in this note:
- Can you confirm the preferred production maintenance window for canary (propose: Sat 0200–0600 PT)?
- Any hard blackout dates between Dec 20–Jan 5 we should avoid for training or migration?
- Procurement required doc: have you completed the SOC2 self-attestation — we asked for evidence in the contract. If available, please attach.

I'm looping in Marissa & Jonas for technical scheduling and Laura for training/acceptance. Next step: quick 30-min sync tomorrow to lock the canary window and training slots so we can publish the MAP.

Attachments: Execution_MAP_v0.1.xlsx, Security_Evidence_Summary.pdf, Training_Roster_v1.csv

Stephanie —

Thanks for the kickoff and the MAP draft. High level: the proposed cadence looks good. Quick answers:
- Maintenance window: Sat 0200–0600 PT works for our ops team.
- Blackout dates: none in Dec, but we have a system freeze on Jan 1–2. Please avoid Jan 1–2 for any cutovers.
- SOC2 evidence: attaching a redacted SOC2 cover + our procurement checklist (Procurement_SOW.pdf). We'll follow up with our security team if you need further artifacts.

One ask from our side: for the canary we need a defined rollback SLA (how fast can you revert to the previous routing if token-level latency or error rate exceeds thresholds?). Put another way, canary acceptance must include token latency < 150ms p50 and error rate < 0.5% over a 30-minute window.

Also copying a short note to the thread: we prefer the canary to run for at least two business days with a gradual ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%) so we can surface any integration issues.

Thanks —
Alex
Director of Platform Ops | PulseSecure Health
alex.chen@pulsesecurehealth.com

Subject: Re: Execution MAP & Canary Runbook — technical canary + rollback plan

Alex / team —

Thanks Alex — great detail on acceptance thresholds. Below is a compact technical runbook proposal that I'll own from Redwood's side. I've added these items to the MAP under Week 3 (Canary).

Canary runbook (high level):
- Canary window: Sat 02:00–06:00 PT (as agreed)
- Duration: 48 hours contiguous (Sat + Sun) with staged ramping: 10% (hour 0–3) -> 30% (hour 3–12) -> 60% (hour 12–36) -> 100% (hour 36–48)
- Monitoring: token p50/p95 latency, error rate, 5m avg for CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit ratio.
- Acceptance: token p50 < 150ms and error rate < 0.5% sustained for a 30-minute rolling window.
- Rollback policy: automatic traffic shift back to previous model variant if any of the acceptance metrics breach for 15 continuous minutes. Manual rollback option for operations with a target RTO of 10 minutes.
- Communication: Ops channel (PulseSecure: #psh-canary) + Redwood runbook Slack alerts + paging to on-call if breach persists.

Migration notes:
- Migration cutover to run in Week 5 during a 4-hour window; pre-cutover smoke tests in Staging and a dry-run one week earlier.
- Data sync: incremental sync overnight for 3 days before cutover, full validation on day-of.

Open items for PulseSecure:
- Confirm the identity of the PulseSecure on-call for canary (name + mobile).
- Confirm whether you want a warm-standby rollback (we can keep the old endpoint active for immediate traffic diversion).

I'll attach a short technical appendix to the MAP and update Execution_MAP_v1 after we lock the on-call and rollback preference.

-Marissa
Implementation Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Execution MAP & Canary Runbook — training, evals, and acceptance criteria

Alex / Marissa / Stephanie —

Thanks — quick note from the Enablement side. I reviewed the MAP and added a training and evaluation plan that maps to the canary and migration milestones. Summary:
- Training: two instructor-led sessions (Ops runbook walkthrough + SRE troubleshooting) during Week 2; recorded playbacks available.
- Eval plan: we will run three prompt-set regressions across dev/staging/prod (minimal 200 samples each) and track quality deltas. Pass criteria: no regression > 3% mean relative accuracy drop vs baseline. Dataset and scripts are in eval_prompt_set.csv (linked in the MAP).
- Acceptance gate: sign-off requires Ops on-call to complete a staged runbook drill in Staging and SRE to validate latency/error targets.

Open for PulseSecure: please confirm two training attendees (names + emails) so I can enroll them and produce completion certs.

Cheers —
Laura Bennett

Thank you all for the quick responses. Per the thread we've agreed the following and I've updated Execution_MAP_v1.xlsx (attached + Drive link):
